purpose: Bounded Fair Work Commission case linking regular-casual work, customer/service conflict, neurodivergence disclosure, abrupt dismissal, and an unfair-dismissal finding while preserving the unresolved remedy and later-work stages.

events.geography: Perth, Western Australia; Fair Work Commission U2024/9845
events.date_precision: employment ran February 2023 to dismissal on 1 August 2024; decision dated 24 February 2025
events.denominator: One publicly adjudicated worker case; no population denominator
events.method: Structured extraction from the primary Fair Work Commission decision [2025] FWC 561
events.missingness: Private payroll and household records, exact lost earnings, remedy outcome, payment or reinstatement, alternative work, and later livelihood are not retained
events.exposure: A regular casual nail technician worked every week, usually 16 to 23 hours, and was dismissed after disputed complaints about client service, language, booking changes, and service timing
events.alternatives_before_action: The public record does not identify another job, household buffer, client-base alternative, or practical substitute income before the application
events.immediate_burden_or_benefit: Dismissal removed a regular and systematic work route; the decision also records that the worker disclosed neurodivergence and masking difficulties, while the employer did not give a formal warning or opportunity to respond before dismissal
events.choice_or_response: The worker represented herself, supplied payslips and messages, challenged jurisdiction and fairness, and pursued the unfair-dismissal remedy route
events.person_or_actor_with_control: The employer controlled roster, client allocation, warnings, and dismissal; the worker controlled evidence and application; the Commission controlled the jurisdictional and fairness finding and later remedy process
events.remedy_or_institutional_response: The Commission found the worker was a regular casual protected by the unfair-dismissal jurisdiction and that the dismissal was harsh, unjust, and unreasonable; remedy was deferred for further evidence and conciliation
events.remedy_receipt: No payment, reinstatement, compensation, or settlement is established in this merits decision
events.durability_followup: The public record reaches the unfair-dismissal finding but not the later remedy, return, alternative employment, earnings recovery, or trust outcome
events.immediate_outcome: The worker obtained a formal unfair-dismissal finding, while the practical remedy remained unresolved in the decision
events.protected_outcome: The decision protected recognition of regular-casual status and procedural fairness at the adjudication stage; income continuity and future work were not yet protected
events.sacrificed_outcome: The worker lost a regular work route and carried the evidence and application burden; household, health, and later-career effects are unknown
events.cost_risk_transfer: The employer's dismissal shifted income and procedural risk to the worker; the Commission route shifted legal accountability back toward the employer without yet establishing practical recovery
events.later_outcome: The official decision records an unfair-dismissal finding and directs a separate remedy process; no later payment, return, replacement work, household recovery, trust, or exit endpoint is public in this record
events.meaning_and_attribution: The case connects service-performance judgment and neurodivergence/masking to a disputed employment decision; the Commission attributes unfairness to lack of valid reason and procedural fairness, not to a standardized cultural meaning measure
events.public_or_collective_response: Individual self-represented tribunal participation is observed; no collective or political response is reported
events.counterexample: A worker can have regular hours and a formal unfair-dismissal finding while practical income restoration and remedy receipt remain unresolved
events.source_and_uncertainty: Primary Fair Work Commission decision [2025] FWC 561, https://www.fwc.gov.au/documents/decisionssigned/pdf/2025fwc561.pdf; the decision establishes the merits finding and deferred remedy process but not later implementation

arrows.from: regular casual work and disputed service-performance conflict
arrows.to: dismissal without formal warning or adequate opportunity to respond
arrows.evidence: The decision records weekly regular work, disputed complaints, dismissal on 1 August 2024, and no valid reason or procedural fairness
arrows.counterexample: A complaint record does not itself establish that dismissal was necessary or that another job was available
arrows.remaining_gap: Prior warnings, employer comparison, alternative work, and household buffer

arrows.evidence: The Commission examined 85 payslips, found weekly regular and systematic work, and held that the worker was protected by the jurisdiction
arrows.counterexample: Legal recognition of status does not restore lost shifts or income
arrows.remaining_gap: Lost earnings, benefits, replacement work, and practical access

arrows.to: separate remedy process and conciliation direction
arrows.evidence: The Commission found unfair dismissal and stated that neither party supplied enough material to determine remedy, directing further submissions and member-assisted conciliation
arrows.counterexample: A successful merits finding can still leave remedy amount, timing, and form undecided
arrows.remaining_gap: Remedy amount, payment or reinstatement, receipt, adequacy, and implementation

arrows.to: later livelihood, trust, recovery, switching, or exit
arrows.evidence: The decision ends before the separate remedy process and does not report later employment or household outcomes
arrows.counterexample: Recognition of procedural unfairness is not the same as restored income, dignity, or durable work access
arrows.remaining_gap: Final remedy, receipt, alternative work, earnings, health, household security, trust, recurrence, and exit

boundary: This ledger adds a contemporary small-firm and neurodivergence-sensitive employment case that closes regular-work exposure through merits adjudication but leaves the practical remedy and later livelihood stages open.
storage_boundary: No private payroll, medical, household, client, or employment file is retained; only bounded public decision fields, dates, findings, uncertainty, and open downstream arrows are represented.
